customer_name: Huace Film & TV Group (华策影视集团)
business_problem: Huace Film & TV needed to accelerate script and media-production work without sacrificing output quality. Creative teams had to summarize and evaluate long texts, translate scripts and dialogue across languages, and identify or clip relevant video scenes, but doing that manually slowed early-stage creation and project preparation.
solution_summary: Huace Film & TV deployed an intelligent screenplay-creation assistance system on Alibaba Cloud Bailian so creative teams could treat large models as part of day-to-day production rather than isolated experiments. Qwen-based model capability is used on long-text script workloads, where writers and reviewers need fast summarization, structured outlines, and script-evaluation output in consistent formats. The same system also supports multilingual translation of scripts and dialogue, while reducing the length limits that make generic model use impractical for full production documents. Huace is extending the same architecture into video workflows for scene recognition, automated tagging, clip extraction, and intelligent editing so long-form drama assets can be repurposed more efficiently. By centralizing writer assistance, evaluation, translation, and media-processing scenarios on Bailian, Huace created a reusable AI production stack for television, film, and short-drama teams.

solution_components.name: Bailian
solution_components.role: Provides the large-model service platform that hosts Huace's script and media AI workloads.

solution_components.name: Qwen models
solution_components.role: Handle summarization, script evaluation, translation, and other core creative-language tasks.

solution_components.name: intelligent screenplay creation assistance system
solution_components.role: Delivers writer assistance, script evaluation, and related media-processing workflows to production teams.

data_flow: Scripts, dialogue, and other long-text materials are sent into the Bailian and Qwen layer for summarization, evaluation, and translation. The resulting outputs are consumed by Huace production teams and extended into downstream scene-recognition, clip-extraction, and intelligent-editing workflows for film and television assets.
integration_points: television, film, and short-drama production teams
business_outcome: Huace accelerated early-stage creation and review without lowering output quality. Writers can generate ideas, adapt scenes and dialogue, and produce script-analysis outlines within minutes, while evaluation workflows shorten project-preparation cycles and the shared LLM foundation opens the same production pipeline to video clipping and editing scenarios across film, television, and short-drama teams.
architecture_clues: The same LLM platform spans script summarization, evaluation, translation, and downstream media-processing scenarios.
Long-text support is a key requirement because screenplay and dialogue workflows exceed the practical limits of generic ad hoc prompting.
Huace is using one AI foundation across television, film, and short-drama production teams rather than isolated pilot projects.
